args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The same version had also been unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Checked after rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and review why a release that failed in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Why v2.3.0:** It's the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rolling back to it didn't need change-manager approval, since that's only required for versions that have never been healthy in production.
- **Now:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the checks after it. It lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed before deploying it again, and look into why it reached production. Its staging build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
